identity.fantasy: A dual-wielding earthen juggernaut who turns rapid weapon procs into instant earthquakes, hammers, barriers, and avatar-sized control.
identity.one_line: A Stamina-scaling earth tank with Quake, hammers, pulls, Aftershock procs, Earthen Avatar, and heavy frontal control. Recent builds and reports consistently praise its dungeon durability and solo capability, though logs are still too young for a durable ranking.

mechanics.core_loop: Dual wield fast weapons to trigger Aftershock-style effects, keep Quake active for area threat, use Mountain Hammer and Terrasmash for focused control, spend excess procs on Geode only when Quake coverage and Rage permit, and rotate Earthen Avatar, barriers, and Call of the Mountain around dangerous pulls.
mechanics.single_target: Maintain the proc engine and hammer priority while preserving defensive avatar and barrier timing for boss swings.
mechanics.aoe: Instant Quake refreshes, Earthbreaker, frontal hammers, pulls, and later Seismic Smash make large grouped pulls the specialization's clearest strength.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Roll and Primalist mobility help reposition; area effects live around the tank, so target switching is less costly than losing the pack's grouping.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Mountain Giant, Stone Skin, Earthen Avatar, Earthenforged Barrier, Call of the Mountain, and heavy frontal control create strong physical durability.
mechanics.group_utility: Pulls, stuns, bellow effects, armor, and stable area threat support fast dungeon pacing.

failure_modes.text: Spending an instant-earthquake proc on Geode when Quake is about to fall can cost area threat and mitigation rhythm.

Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: roll and primalist mobility help reposition; area effects live around the tank, so target switching is less costly than losing the pack's grouping.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: mountain giant, stone skin, earthen avatar, earthenforged barrier, call of the mountain, and heavy frontal control create strong physical durability.

You enjoy the spec's core cadence: dual wield fast weapons to trigger aftershock-style effects, keep quake active for area threat, use mountain hammer and terrasmash for focused control, spend excess procs on geode only when quake coverage and rage permit, and rotate earthen avatar, barriers, and call of the mountain around dangerous pulls.

avoid_if.text: You want traditional sword-and-shield tanking or dislike proc-driven defensive pacing.
You dislike the positioning or swap constraint that roll and primalist mobility help reposition; area effects live around the tank, so target switching is less costly than losing the pack's grouping.

praise.theme: Recent players consistently praise Mountain King's dungeon durability, solo pulling, aesthetics, and frequent instant Earthquakes.

frustrations.theme: Players warn that two-handers reduce proc frequency and that Geode can waste a global or proc when Rage is already healthy.

gaps: Magic-damage weakness and capstone choices need encounter-specific evidence.

claims.text: A July weapon discussion says Mountain King should dual wield because fast attacks generate frequent Aftershock procs for instant Quake. Players recommend refreshing Quake about every nine seconds and using spare procs on Geode only when Rage and Quake timing justify it.
claims.notes: Community working guidance, not controlled weapon testing.

claims.text: Recent Primalist players describe Mountain King as highly durable, capable of massive solo pulls, easy dungeon tanking, high physical resistance, and strong battleground flag carrying, while warning that strong casters remain a weakness.
claims.notes: Self-selected player reports.

claims.text: The August Mythic inventory lists 93 Mountain King records. The DPS compilation's 1,661 value is explicitly off-role tank DPS and must not be treated as tank strength.
claims.notes: Representation is not mitigation or power.

claims.text: Mountain King's central decision is routing frequent instant-earth procs between mandatory Quake coverage and optional Rage or damage payoffs without compromising defense.
claims.notes: Exact proc name is community shorthand and should be verified against the current base class kit.
